scientific_rubric.description: Identity and scope: State the model composition, electron count, charge, electronic description and relation to the experimental dimer. A bonding explanation needs electronic evidence beyond a bond length. If comparing deformations or fragments, keep composition, state, reference and constraints consistent and distinguish minima from saddles.

Quantitative scientific results: Establish a quantitative, physically sound molecular description of the observed metal–metal bonding using correct stoichiometry and a justified model. Full210-atom computation is not mandatory when a smaller representation demonstrably addresses the bounded claim.

Evidence that distinguishes the claimed explanation: Support the proposed electronic/structural explanation with discriminating evidence. Orbital, density, energetic or other justified analyses can qualify; no prescribed orbital labels, deformation grid or fragment charge partition is required.

Uncertainty and limits: Assess whether model truncation, state stability and relevant numerical/relativistic assumptions limit the interpretation. Claimed minima/saddles and energetic comparisons require evidence appropriate to their structural status.

Bounded answer to the question: Provide or delimit an evidence-based explanation for the observed short bond and the validity of the chosen model. A reference bond length, nominal bond-order number or visually attractive orbital without supporting analysis is insufficient.

scoring_notes: AR and PR share result validity; actual open_research runtime supplies mode-specific process rubrics.
Source author outcomes are conditional reference evidence, not mandatory winners. No inherited numerical tolerance.
No penalty simply for a different justified model, hypothesis count, metric or valid analysis route. Scientific adequacy is claim-dependent.
Completion requires a substantiated answer to the stated question. Honest partial credit is distinct from passing all scientific criteria.
